info.title: ZeroGPU API
info.description:
REST API for ZeroGPU model inference: `POST /v1/responses` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` (model-dependent).
Authenticate every request with the `x-api-key` header or, OpenAI-compatible, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The `x-project-id` header is optional.
Documentation: https://docs.zerogpu.ai

**Per-model playgrounds** are listed on [Model playgrounds](/api-reference/models) with request examples for each model's use cases.
These endpoint pages show a generic shape only.

value.input: NASA announced that its Artemis III mission is now scheduled for late 2026, marking the first time astronauts will land on the lunar surface since Apollo 17 in 1972. The mission will send a crew of four to the Moon aboard the Orion spacecraft, with two astronauts descending to the south pole using SpaceX Starship as a lunar lander. Scientists are particularly excited about exploring permanently shadowed craters that may contain water ice, which could be critical for sustaining long-term human presence on the Moon.

What is the weather in Paris right now?

ApiKey.name: x-api-key
ApiKey.description: Your ZeroGPU API key. Create one in the dashboard under API keys. Send it on every request.

BearerAuth.description: OpenAI-compatible: send your ZeroGPU API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

model.description: Model identifier. Open a [model page](/api-reference/models) for a dedicated playground with the correct body for that model.

input.description: The text or document to send, as a plain string. To return a tool result, send an array of input items instead: the conversation so far, the model's `function_call` item, and a `function_call_output` item with the same `call_id`.

stream.description: If `true`, the response is sent as server-sent events (`text/event-stream`) instead of one JSON body. See [Streaming](/api-reference/responses#streaming) for the events. Supported on text-generation models; task models (classifiers, extractors) return `400` with code `stream_not_supported`.

tools.description: Function tools the model may call. When it calls one, `output` contains a `function_call` item; see [Tool calling](/api-reference/responses#tool-calling). Models without tool support return `400` with code `tools_not_supported`.

type.description: Output format for the response, for example `text`.

instructions.description: Optional system-style instructions applied on top of `input`, for models that support them.

metadata.description: Optional model-specific parameters, passed through to the model. For example, the GLiNER2.5 models accept `usecase` together with `labels` or `schema`. See the relevant [model page](/api-reference/models) for supported keys.

model.description: Model identifier. Open a [model page](/api-reference/models) for a dedicated playground with the correct body for that model.

messages.description: Ordered list of messages making up the conversation so far.

metadata.description: Optional model-specific parameters, passed through to the model. For example, the GLiNER2.5 models accept `usecase` together with `labels` or `schema`. See the relevant [model page](/api-reference/models) for supported keys.

created.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the completion was created.

index.description: Position of this choice in the list.

finish_reason.description: Why the model stopped generating, for example `stop` or `length`.

ChatUsage.description: Token usage statistics for the request.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the prompt.

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the generated completion.

created.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the response was created.

output.description: Output items produced by the model: `message` items, and a `function_call` item for each tool the model calls. Reasoning models may also return a `reasoning` item. Read items by `type`, not by position.

OutputMessage.description: A single output item from the model.

content.description: Content parts that make up the message.

text.example: Artemis III, slated for late 2026, will return astronauts to the Moon for the first time since 1972.

Usage.description: Token usage statistics for the request.

input_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the input.

FunctionTool.description: A function the model may call.

name.description: Function name the model uses to call it.

description.description: What the function does. The model uses this to decide when to call it.
description.example: Get the current weather for a city.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the function's arguments.

role.description: Author of the message, for example `user`.

FunctionCall.title: Function call
FunctionCall.description: A tool call made by the model. Returned in `output`; send it back unchanged in `input` together with its `function_call_output`.

call_id.description: ID that links this call to its `function_call_output`.

name.description: Name of the function to call.

arguments.description: Arguments as a JSON-encoded string. Parse it before use.

FunctionCallOutput.title: Function call output
FunctionCallOutput.description: The result of a tool call, sent back to the model.

output.description: The tool result as a string, for example JSON.

ResponseStreamEvent.description: One server-sent event of a streamed response. Each event is sent as a `data:` line holding this JSON object; most models end the stream with `data: [DONE]`.

sequence_number.description: Position of the event in the stream, starting at 0.

output_index.description: Index of the output item the event belongs to.

item_id.description: ID of the output item the event belongs to.

delta.description: On `*.delta` events: the next chunk of text or function arguments.

text.description: On `response.output_text.done`: the full text of the content part.

item.description: On `response.output_item.added` and `.done`: the output item (`message` or `function_call`).

response.description: On `response.created`, `response.in_progress` and `response.completed`: the response object. On `response.completed` it holds the full `output` and `usage`.

ErrorResponse.description: Error payload returned on a failed request.

message.example: You have insufficient quota to complete this request.

model.description: Moderation model to use. Defaults to the configured moderation model; OpenAI ids (`omni-moderation-latest`, `text-moderation-stable`) are accepted and mapped to it.

input.description: Text to classify. A single string, an array of strings (one result per element), or an array of content parts (`{ "type": "text", "text": "..." }`) forming one multi-modal input.

ModerationCategories.description: Per-category boolean verdicts. All 13 categories are always present, in OpenAI's order.

harassment.description: Content that expresses, incites, or promotes harassing language towards any target.

harassment/threatening.description: Harassment that also includes violence or serious harm towards any target.

hate.description: Content that expresses, incites, or promotes hate based on a protected attribute.

hate/threatening.description: Hateful content that also includes violence or serious harm towards a protected group.

illicit.description: Content that gives advice or instruction on how to commit a wrongdoing.

illicit/violent.description: Illicit content that also references violence or procuring a weapon.

self-harm.description: Content that promotes, encourages, or depicts acts of self-harm.

self-harm/intent.description: Content where the speaker expresses that they are engaging or intend to engage in self-harm.

self-harm/instructions.description: Content that provides instructions or advice on how to commit acts of self-harm.

sexual.description: Content meant to arouse sexual excitement or that promotes sexual services.

sexual/minors.description: Sexual content that includes an individual under 18 years old.

violence.description: Content that depicts death, violence, or physical injury.

violence/graphic.description: Content that depicts death, violence, or physical injury in graphic detail.

ModerationCategoryScores.description: Per-category confidence scores in [0, 1]. All 13 categories are always present, in OpenAI's order.

ModerationAppliedInputTypes.description: Which input modality triggered each category. This is a text-only model, so every category maps to ["text"].

ModerationResult.description: A single entry of the `results` array — the verdict for one input.

flagged.description: True when the model flagged the input in one or more categories.

ModerationResponse.description: OpenAI-compatible moderations envelope. One `results` entry per input.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation request.

results.description: Moderation verdicts, one per input (a string input yields a single-element array).

model.description: Embedding model to use. Embedding models are routable only on this endpoint.

input.description: Text to embed. A single string, or an array of strings (one vector per element). Inputs are truncated at the model's max token length.

index.description: Position of the input this vector was produced from.

embedding.description: The embedding vector. 384 dimensions for both models.

EmbeddingUsage.description: Embeddings are billed on input tokens only; there are no output tokens.

language.description: ISO-639-1 code, such as `en`. Detected automatically when omitted.

prompt.description: Text to guide spelling and style, such as names or jargon.

CreateSpeechRequest.description: JSON body, as the OpenAI SDKs send it. Use `multipart/form-data` to attach a `voice_sample`.

input.example: Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?
input.description: The text to speak. Inline tags such as `[laugh]` and `[cough]` add paralinguistic cues.

voice.description: OpenAI voice names are accepted and all map to the built-in voice.

response_format.description: `pcm` is raw 16-bit little-endian mono at 24 kHz.

CreateSpeechMultipartRequest.description: Multipart form, required for voice cloning.

input.example: Testing model to generate voice. Hey how are you today?
input.description: The text to speak. Inline tags such as `[laugh]` and `[cough]` add paralinguistic cues.

voice.description: OpenAI voice names are accepted and all map to the built-in voice.

response_format.description: `pcm` is raw 16-bit little-endian mono at 24 kHz.

voice_sample.description: Reference clip to clone a voice from. Overrides `voice`. Not stored.

model.description: A model that supports System One: `zlm-v1-moderation-edge`, `zlm-v1-iab-classify-edge`, `zlm-v1-iab-domain-classifier` or `zlm-v2-iab-classify-edge-enriched`.

state.description: The content every question refers to: a string, object or array. An object or array is read as its JSON. For `zlm-v1-iab-domain-classifier` it must be a URL or domain.

questions.description: Named questions (up to 16). Keys are names you choose; each answer comes back under the same key.

instructions.description: The statement or question to evaluate.

criteria.description: Optional definitions of what counts as true and false.

true.description: Free-form text: a string, or an object or array that is read as its JSON.

false.description: Free-form text: a string, or an object or array that is read as its JSON.

instructions.description: Free-form text: a string, or an object or array that is read as its JSON.

criteria.description: Choice names mapped to descriptions. A null description means the name alone is used.

additionalProperties.description: Free-form text: a string, or an object or array that is read as its JSON.

criteria.description: Ordered level descriptions. A level's position is its score, starting at 0.

answers.description: Keyed by your question names, in request order.

noul.description: Probability of true. Near 1 favors true, near 0 favors false, near 0.5 is uncertain.

probabilities.description: Keyed by choice name; sums to about 1.

score.description: Probability-weighted average level; may fall between integers.

legend.description: Level key ("0", "1", ...) to its criteria text.

input_tokens.description: Tokens billed: the state plus the questions.

output_tokens.description: Always 0; System One output is not billed.

HTTPValidationError.description: Request validation failure (System One's own error shape).
